Do the two tables match?

Source: R/summary.R
is_matching.Rd

TRUE when every record of a diff_table() result is same: no value changed and no row is found in only one table. Two empty tables match.

is_matching(d, tolerance = NULL, rel_tol = NULL)

Arguments

d

A result of diff_table().

tolerance, rel_tol

NULL (the default) keeps the thresholds of the comparison. A number re-judges the values: a value matches when within either. When only one is given, the other is 0.

Value

TRUE or FALSE.

Details

With tolerance or rel_tol given, the values are judged again at those thresholds instead of the ones diff_table() used, from the abs_diff and rel_diff it stores. That works in both directions, looser or stricter, so one comparison can be asked at several thresholds without being run again. The rule is diff_table()'s: two equal or two missing values always match, and the tolerances apply to finite pairs only. A row found in only one table never matches, whatever the threshold.

Examples

x <- data.frame(id = 1:3, amount = c(100, 200, 300))
y <- data.frame(id = 1:3, amount = c(100, 200.5, 300))
d <- diff_table(x, y)
is_matching(d)
#> [1] FALSE
is_matching(d, tolerance = 1)
#> [1] TRUE
is_matching(d, rel_tol = 0.001)
#> [1] FALSE
is_matching(d, rel_tol = 0.01)
#> [1] TRUE
